_about: Public-domain Richard Fuller (1804-1876), Baptist minister of Beaufort and Baltimore, for the Word Hoard: Our Duty to the African Race (1851), Sermons (1860), The Christian Delivered from the Fear of Death (1861) and Mercy Remembered in Wrath (1861), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 53 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

rfuller-african-race: Our duty to the African race. An address delivered at Washington, D. C., January 21, 1851 (Baltimore : Printed by W.M. Innes, 1851)
rfuller-sermons: Sermons (New York, Sheldon & company; Baltimore, Giteau & Sullivan, 1860)
rfuller-fear-of-death: The Christian delivered from the fear of death : a discourse (Baltimore : Printed by W.M. Innes, 1861)
rfuller-mercy-remembered: Mercy remembered in wrath : a sermon preached by the Rev. Dr. Fuller, on Thursday, September 26, 1861, being the day of national fasting, humiliation and prayer (Henry Taylor, 1861)

_excluded.rfuller-other: The Psalmist hymn book (1843, he co-edited); Chaplain Fuller (1863, about Arthur Fuller, another man)

_identity_checked.rfuller-african-race: Title page OCR reads 'Our Duty to the African Race. An Address Delivered at Washington, D. C., January 21, 1851, BY R^IOHA-JiilJ FULLER' (Richard garbled); the preface names 'Rev. Dr. Fuller' introduced by Mr. Clay. Baltimore: W. M. Innes.
_identity_checked.rfuller-mercy-remembered: Title page reads 'Preached by the Rev. Dr. Fuller ... BALTIMORE: PUBLISHED BY HENRY TAYLOR ... 1861. W. M. INNES, Printer'. Richard Fuller was the Baltimore Baptist pastor in 1861; same printer as his signed 1851 address. Not Thomas Fuller (d. 1661).
